title: Lessons from Max Roach and inspiration from artists who kept creating
summary: Jang reflects on Roach's final years, concerts in 2001-02, and elders who created into old age, and Picasso's remark about becoming young.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: undemocratic. So anyway there’s so much that I’ve learned from Max Roach, and it helped validate the direction of where I’m going and who I am. So it’s taken me years to reflect. And also I had to realize, or learn to realize, because of lot of us, like our heroes when we’re young, that I had a friendship but also a friendship with someone who — you know when you think about heroes there’s this immortality and they’re perfect. But we all have problems. And one of them was deteriorating health. But what inspired me was that hey, he was in his 70’s. And the concert we did in Milano, Italy was incredible, in 2001. And then in 2002 in Los Angeles, I mean I couldn’t believe — he was like I think Max Roach described it he says it’s like I never stopped learning to ride the bicycle. It was like he was in his 20’s or 30’s or 40’s, still he was the great Max Roach. And my goals, now that I’m approaching 60 years of age, I’m inspired by Max Roach to pursue, pursue, pursue. I’m inspired by Duke Ellington, who was composing music on his deathbed. I’m inspired by Giuseppe Verdi, who wrote full staff, an opera, a comic opera, when he was 80 years old, or Akira Kurosawa, who was making his last film in his 80’s, or Pablo Casals, who I think he recorded some Bach suites in his 90’s and he said he was practicing and he finally learned how to play them right, or something outrageous like that. And you know, it brings to me Pablo Picasso. The English translation of what he said, he said it takes a long time to become young. And what he was talking about is everyone knows well who was the first president of the United States, two and two is equal to four, or from some Asians who are really great in math, the quadratic formula, which you’ve got to fit in a circle, what’s the opposite of B plus or minus — well why is it either/or you know? The opposite of B, plus or minus the square root of B square minus 4AC over 2A. You know? But Pablo Picasso was talking about discovering what’s unique about you in your planet. There’s only one Jon Jang. So it’s about the music of Jon Jang. The changing music of Jon Jang. There’s the music of Max Roach. There’s the music of Monk Rowe. You know, that’s when I say Thelonious Monk — always? No. Always Rowe. Monk? Always Rowe? No?
